references.text: Paul quotes directly from Deuteronomy 27:26 in Galatians to show that all who rely on the works of the law are under a curse, because no one can keep the whole law.
Jeremiah refers to the covenant curse upon those who do not obey the words of this covenant, reflecting the curse in Deuteronomy 27:26.
This verse continues the theme of curses on those who do not keep the Lord's commands and statutes, expanding on the curse from 27:26.
The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping all the words of this law, with consequences for those who fail to do so.
The curses in this book of the covenant will fall upon anyone who does not uphold the words of the law, further developing the theme from 27:26.
Joshua read aloud all the words of the law, both the blessing and the curse, in accordance with what is written in the Book of the Law.
The people committed themselves to keeping God's law and took an oath with a curse if they failed to keep it.
James teaches that whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at one point is guilty of breaking all of it—a principle that reflects the curse in Deuteronomy 27:26.
